title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript note. It is a typed page, p. 175 of an Exposé IX, with a printed-volume page number 493 stamped at the bottom. It appears to have been filed among the 1976 De Rham p.d. notes. The content matches the 'transcendental' part of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), Springer LNM 288, where Exp. IX occupies roughly pp. 313–523; the match is my identification, not stated on the page.

Setting: S is a complex analytic space (a disc-like neighbourhood of a point s). A is a commutative analytic group over S, presented via the dictionary 13.1.4 as A = E/R, where:
- E is the Lie-algebra vector bundle;
- R is a family of discrete 'period' subgroups;
- R^t ⊂ R^f ⊂ R are respectively the toric part and the 'fixed' part of the period lattice.

The exact sequence (13.3.15), 0 → R^f/R^t → E/E^t → B → 0, defines the quotient B = A/T of A by the torus T = E^t/R^t. Since R^f/R^t = (R_0/R_0^t)_S is a constant analytic group over S (13.3.16), criterion 13.1.5 applies. It says B is an abeloid group (a family of complex tori, not necessarily algebraic) near s if and only if its fibre B_0 = A_0/T_0 is abeloid.

Consequence (the underlined statement): any way of writing the special fibre A_0 as an extension of an abeloid group by a complex torus extends uniquely, near s, to an extension structure (13.3.13) of A by T with abeloid quotient B. This is a rigidity/deformation statement for 'semi-abeloid' structures.

§13.4 then begins to recast the dictionary in terms of Deligne's mixed Hodge structures. Let \underline{R} be the sheaf of sections of R and set ℰ(A) = \underline{R} ⊗_ℤ O_S. This is locally free of finite type when R is locally constant, and in general need not be coherent. The map \underline{R} → \underline{E} (13.1.3) is about to define a Hodge-type filtration. The purpose is to describe degenerating families of complex tori via variations of mixed Hodge structure of type {(0,0),(0,-1),(-1,0),(-1,-1)}, essentially 1-motive-like data.

ideas.what: Unique extension near s of a torus-by-abeloid extension structure given on the special fibre of an analytic group family
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of semi-abelian (semi-abeloid) structures in families; degeneration of complex tori
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exp. IX §13 (LNM 288), as identified from the typescript

ideas.what: Reformulating the analytic-group dictionary as variations of mixed Hodge structure via ℰ = R ⊗ O_S
ideas.modern_name: Variations of mixed Hodge structure of level ≤1 / Hodge realization of 1-motives

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript of published material, apparently SGA 7 Exp. IX (page stamp 493 fits LNM 288), misfiled among the 1976 De Rham p.d. notes. Nothing on it is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: 'soit ℝ le faisceau' should read underlined R (\underline{R}, the sheaf of sections of R), not the blackboard-bold reals.
The bottom number 493 is a page number in the published volume, not part of the text; the internal typescript page is 175 of Exposé IX.
